documents.unit: Student Code of Conduct (Worldwide student handbook page)
documents.title: Student Code of Conduct: Academic Integrity, Artificial Intelligence (AI)
documents.stance_why: The section says 'Students may use AI to support learning and productivity when its use is consistent with course objectives, assignment requirements, and instructor or supervisor directions' and bans use 'in violation of University, program, course or instructor requirements'. It sets no uniform rule itself and defers to course and instructor, so delegates.
documents.summary: The handbook's academic-integrity section lists AI misuse as a violation and encourages AI fluency, while permitting AI for learning when consistent with course and instructor rules. It gives examples of appropriate uses and a duty to verify output, and defers disclosure and restrictions to syllabus statements.

units.why: This defines AI misuse as an integrity violation: 'in violation of University, program, course or instructor requirements, including unauthorized use'. Classified as misconduct, so P36.
units.anchor: Using artificial intelligence or automated technologies in violation of University, program, course or instructor requirements

units.why: Lists 'misrepresentation of AI-generated work' as a violation; passing AI output off as one's own is the nondisclosure-as-violation idea in P28, rather than the general misconduct class P36 used for the neighbouring items.
units.resolution_why: Coder A merged misrepresentation and fabrication into one P36 unit; coder B split them and gave misrepresentation P28 and the rest P36. The source lists them as separate forms of misuse in one sentence, so one rule per unit is followed. Misrepresenting AI-generated work is the failure-to-disclose violation that P28 covers, whereas the other forms are plain misconduct, so B's split is kept.

units.why: Names 'fabrication or falsification of information' through AI as a violation; a form of misconduct, hence P36.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B split this out (coder A merged it with misrepresentation under one anchor). The source names fabrication or falsification of information as a distinct violation, so it is kept as a P36 unit.

units.why: Names 'use of AI to facilitate other prohibited conduct' as a violation; misconduct class, P36.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B split this out (coder A did not code it separately). The source names use of AI to facilitate other prohibited conduct as a distinct violation, so it is kept as P36.
units.anchor: use of AI to facilitate other prohibited conduct

units.why: Sets the guiding principle for all educational AI use ('must be guided by ethical principles and academic integrity'), an institution-level framework statement, P56.
units.resolution_why: Both coders: P56, general, must, neutral. Topics differ (A: default-stance, policy-evolution; B: ethics-bias-environment, default-stance). The source says use 'must be guided by ethical principles and academic integrity', so B's ethics topic fits better than policy-evolution.
units.anchor: must be guided by ethical principles and academic integrity

units.why: Expresses the university's welcome of AI skill-building: 'encourages students to develop fluency in artificial intelligence'. Framed as professional development, so P44 rather than a default-permit rule (P02), which the next permission unit covers.
units.anchor: encourages students to develop fluency in artificial intelligence

units.why: 'students are expected to engage thoughtfully and responsibly with these technologies' is a general expectation of responsible use, a framework principle (P56) rather than a specific permitted or prohibited use.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A found this. Source: 'students are expected to engage thoughtfully and responsibly with these technologies as part of their academic and professional development.' It is a real expectation distinct from the encouragement sentence, a general responsible-use principle, so P56 with should is kept.
units.anchor: students are expected to engage thoughtfully and responsibly with these technologies

units.why: States the default permission with conditions: 'Students may use AI to support learning and productivity when its use is consistent with course objectives'. Allowed by default but bounded by course rules, so P02.
units.anchor: Students may use AI to support learning and productivity

units.why: Requires that AI 'strengthen, and not replace, the student's own understanding, judgment, intellectual effort'; students remain the primary thinker, P32.
units.anchor: AI use should strengthen, and not replace, the student’s own understanding

units.why: First listed appropriate use: 'Clarifying difficult concepts or receiving explanations', AI as a tutor, P12.
units.anchor: Clarifying difficult concepts or receiving explanations.

units.why: 'Practicing language, coding or problem-solving skills' is a practice use of AI; P14 fits better than P13 since debugging is not mentioned.
units.anchor: Practicing language, coding or problem-solving skills.

units.why: 'Creating non-graded examples, scenarios or visuals to support learning' is a study-aid use, P14; the 'non-graded' qualifier leaves graded work uncovered.
units.anchor: Creating non-graded examples, scenarios or visuals to support learning.

units.why: 'Supporting course learning activities where permitted by the instructor' makes AI use depend on the instructor, so P04.
units.anchor: Supporting course learning activities where permitted by the instructor.

units.why: Students 'are responsible for evaluating and verifying any material produced' by AI, including fabricated citations; a verification duty, P31.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P31, student, must, during-work but differed on unit_stance (A neutral, B require). The passage requires checking AI output for errors; that is a duty of care, not a requirement to use AI, so neutral.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for evaluating and verifying any material produced, summarized, transformed or suggested

units.why: 'Use of AI must comply with: Embry-Riddle's Academic Integrity Policy' ties AI use to the existing integrity policy; it is a scope/framework rule, P56.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A found this. Source: 'Use of AI must comply with: Embry-Riddle's Academic Integrity Policy'. It is a real compliance rule tying AI use to the existing integrity policy; a scope/framework rule, so P56 as coded by A is kept.
units.anchor: Use of AI must comply with:

units.why: AI use 'must comply with' IT and data security policies and points to AI Resources; data protection and vetted-tool guidance, P50.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P50, must, during-work; unit_stance differed (A neutral, B restrict) and anchors differed in length. Source: 'Use of AI must comply with ... IT and data security policies.' It requires compliance and does not limit which AI uses are allowed, so neutral. A's fuller anchor is used.
units.anchor: IT and data security policies. For more information, see Embry-Riddle AI Resources.

units.why: AI use must comply with course guidelines 'including expectations for disclosure and labeling of AI-generated content'; disclosure with submissions, P24.
units.anchor: including expectations for disclosure and labeling of AI-generated content

units.why: Students are 'responsible for understanding and following any instructor-specific restrictions on AI use', so rules vary by instructor, P04.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for understanding and following any instructor-specific restrictions on AI use.

units.why: Defines fraud to include 'the unauthorized use of AI technology' to gain unfair advantage; misconduct class, P36.
units.anchor: including the unauthorized use of AI technology

notes: Reconciled from two coders. Only the AI section of the Academic Integrity part of the handbook plus the Fraud line mentioning AI were coded. Dropped as not AI-specific: the baseline 'prepare and present their own work' line and the Cheating line on 'unauthorized assistance, including technology', which never names AI. No school or computing document found; course layer deferred.
